key_insight: Atmospheric plasma spraying produced predominantly crystalline Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings, with spray distance controlling the trade-off between hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: A 90 mm spray distance offered the most favorable tested balance of mechanical performance and electrochemical behavior through a relatively dense, cohesive microstructure.
method: Deposit low-glass-forming-ability Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varied spray distances.
Characterize phases, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behavior.
evidence_signal: XRD detected no amorphous fraction, porosity ranged from 2.2–4.9%, and increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance while reducing corrosion resistance.
watch_item: The 90 mm result is specific to the investigated conditions; longer spray distances can increase porosity and interlamellar defects that compromise corrosion resistance.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
